text:
maya: Heads up — seeing a wave of evictions across ap-southeast1 this morning after the affinity threshold bump. Lots of tiny GPU pods getting squeezed and latebind failures.
kevin: yup, alerting. heatmap shows dense packing on a few racks, then autoscaler trim caused a cascade of preempts. quick snippet from scheduler logs: 
kevin: ```E scheduler: failedFit pod=vision-train-72 node=gpu-rack-17 reason=AffinityConflict score=15```
samir: can you point to the rollout/PR that changed thresholds? wondering if this is correlated to the 06:10 deploy.
maya: it was the affinity-threshold bump in prod flag set: --affinity-threshold=0.75 (was 0.6). I flipped it in the canary yesterday, rolled to prod at 06:05.
lina: that increase makes the scheduler prefer tighter co-location; combined with our aggressive scale-down window it seems to have forced small pods into fewer nodes, then the scaler removed nodes and we got eviction churn. :warning:
ops-bot: autoscaler event: ap-southeast1a scaled down 18 -> 12 at 06:20 (policy=aggressive, reason=cpu undercommit).
kevin: mitigation proposal: rollback the affinity bump, temporarily extend the reserve window to avoid immediate preemptions, and reduce cross-AZ preemption aggressiveness.
maya: agreed. I'm rolling back the flag to 0.6 now and will watch. opened an emergency PR to revert the change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/452 (revert affinity bump) :thumbsup:
samir: I'm pausing autoscaler for ap-southeast1 for 30m to stop further churn. starting now.
lina: can we also run a short simulation against our small-pod trace to validate packing vs cost? want to make sure we don't over-correct and explode unit cost.
kevin: I'll create a canary with soft-affinity=false for pods with GPU<0.5 requests and run the trace. also setting fractional-gang spread=0.15 and reserve-window=90s as a quick guard.
maya: TL;DR: rollback affinity bump, pause scale-downs, patch scheduler to be less aggressive on tiny pods, follow-up postmortem if this repeats.
ops-bot: note: incident channel created #incident-4449998888 — tagging infra oncall.
kevin: thanks — monitoring metrics now (evictions, pending pods, node churn). will post updates every 10m.
lina: adding a short eval to CI to catch future affinity regressions against the small-pod workload.
maya: thanks all, will keep this thread updated.
